name: Mimikatz - Pass the Ticket / OverPass the Hash
description: Injects Kerberos tickets into the current session on Windows. Export tickets with sekurlsa::tickets /export, or dump keys with sekurlsa::ekeys, then either import a .kirbi (ptt) or forge a TGT from a key/hash (OverPass the Hash via sekurlsa::pth).

examples.label: Ch23 - export all tickets to .kirbi files (PEN-200 pattern: steal dave's cifs ticket)
Ch23 - inject a stolen .kirbi ticket into current session then verify with klist

notes: `kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi` injects a Kerberos ticket into the current session; access services as that user without their password. Pair with harvested/forged TGTs. Also covered in: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 23 (Lateral Movement in Active Directory).

references.title: OffSec PEN-200 - Lateral Movement in Active Directory

recommended.note: DCSync once you have a privileged ticket.

defense.why_it_works: Mimikatz kerberos::ptt injects a stolen/forged Kerberos ticket (.kirbi) into the current session so it authenticates as that principal.
defense.prerequisites: A valid/forged Kerberos ticket and a Windows session to inject it into.
defense.impact: Access to services as the ticket's principal without a password (PtT).
defense.detection: [MITRE T1550.003] Anomalous Kerberos activity: a TGS used without a preceding TGT the DC issued; tickets with unusual lifetimes/encryption (RC4 where AES is standard); 4768/4769 anomalies; a ticket used from an unexpected host.
defense.artifacts: A ticket injected into the LSA session (klist shows it); service access as that principal.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4769
| join type=left Account_Name [search index=wineventlog EventCode=4768 | stats count by Account_Name]
| where isnull(count)
| table _time, Computer, Account_Name, Service_Name, Client_Address
defense.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4769
| project rtime=TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, ServiceName, IpAddress
| join kind=leftanti (SecurityEvent | where EventID == 4768 | project TargetUserName) on TargetUserName
| sort by rtime desc
// kerberos::ptt injects a ticket: TGS use without a DC-issued TGT, from an unexpected host
defense.prevention: [MITRE T1550.003 M1026] limit privileged ticket exposure and reset krbtgt (twice) after compromise; enforce AES; monitor for forged/anomalous tickets; Protected Users group for sensitive accounts.
defense.evasion: Passing a legitimately-stolen ticket produces no auth failures and reuses valid Kerberos - realistic ticket lifetimes/AES make it blend with normal traffic.
defense.misconfiguration: Pass-the-Certificate (PtC) attacks exploit ADCS certificate abuse (ESC1/ESC8) combined with Kerberos PKINIT. Shadow credentials (pywhisker) exploit write access to msDS-KeyCredentialLink to add a certificate-based authentication mechanism to any account. Pass-the-Ticket works because Kerberos tickets are extractable from LSASS memory.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# msDS-KeyCredentialLink writable by attacker (GenericWrite on target account):
# pywhisker.py -t targetuser -a add
# Adds a fake device credential -> obtain certificate for targetuser
# -> PKINIT TGT as targetuser -> NTLM hash via UnPAC

# LSASS memory contains TGTs for all logged-in users:
# Mimikatz: sekurlsa::tickets /export
# Rubeus: dump /all
defense.secure_config:
# Prevent msDS-KeyCredentialLink abuse:
# Audit who has GenericWrite on privileged accounts
# Only SYSTEM/DCs should write msDS-KeyCredentialLink
Get-ObjectAcl -Identity admin -ResolveGUIDs | Where-Object {$_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'Write'}

# Prevent ticket extraction:
# Enable Credential Guard (blocks LSASS memory reads)
# Protected Users group members: tickets not cached in LSASS

# ADCS: prevent ESC1/ESC8 (see those cards)
# Monitor: Event 4768 with certificate auth, Event 4769 unusual ticket lifetimes

validation.success_criteria: At least one behavioral detection fires within 60 seconds of attack execution
response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Windows Security Event Log, Sysmon for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Injects a Kerberos ticket into the current Windows session (pass-the-ticket):
  kerberos::ptt <ticket>   load this .kirbi/base64 ticket into the session
Get tickets first with sekurlsa::tickets /export (privilege::debug needed), or dump keys with sekurlsa::ekeys and over-pass-the-hash via sekurlsa::pth. After injection, tools authenticate to services as the ticket's principal.
